recognize_zh: 周邊血液中三個異常細胞的核呈明顯雙葉或摺疊（類似蝴蝶或啞鈴形），細胞質幾乎看不到顆粒、帶淡藍色，符合低顆粒型急性前骨髓性白血病（hypogranular APL, M3v）。
features: Medium to large abnormal cells with moderate N:C ratio
Nuclei deeply folded to bilobed with a central cleft (butterfly/sliding-plate shape)
Pale to moderately basophilic cytoplasm with sparse or no visible azurophilic granules
No Auer rods or faggot cells visible in this field
Background red cells show mild anisocytosis with elongated forms; platelets decreased
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of three abnormal medium-to-large cells with deeply folded, bilobed nuclei imparting a butterfly-like configuration, finely dispersed chromatin, and pale basophilic cytoplasm that is largely devoid of visible granules. Auer rods and faggot cells are not seen in this field. Platelets appear decreased. Findings are suggestive of the hypogranular (microgranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia; urgent confirmation of PML::RARA by FISH or RT-PCR and coagulation studies for DIC are recommended.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts/promonocytes have folded nuclei too, but show more abundant gray-blue cytoplasm, strong nonspecific esterase positivity and are MPO weak, whereas APL cells are strongly MPO positive and HLA-DR/CD34 negative.

ddx.dx: Hairy cell leukemia or other lymphoma with cleaved nuclei
ddx.vs: Lymphoma cells have clumped chromatin and circumferential hairy projections or clefted small nuclei, and lack MPO; flow shows mature B-cell markers.
Classic APL shows dense coarse azurophilic granules obscuring the nucleus and frequent faggot cells, whereas M3v cells appear agranular by light microscopy.
